humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark explicitly targets domain-specific, graduate-level academic expertise across several humanities disciplines (e.g., epigraphic translation in Classics, phonological analysis in Biblical Hebrew, and historical context in Art History) rather than using humanities text merely as raw data for generic language tasks.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Multimodal questions comprising text-only items and items requiring the integration of text with an image reference (representing 14% of the benchmark, such as reading an inscription from an image of a tombstone).
analytical_tasks_explanation: The benchmark includes multiple-choice and exact-match (short-answer) QA testing highly specific domain trivia, factual recall of historical details, epigraphic translation of Palmyrene script from archaeological images, linguistic syllable classification of historical Hebrew texts, and visual reasoning over multimodal source materials.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: HLE is a broad, multi-subject academic benchmark covering over a hundred subjects across STEM, humanities, and social sciences.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates several frontier LLMs including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking, o1, DeepSeek-R1, and o3-mini.

quantitative_metrics.note: Evaluates models using accuracy and RMS calibration error.

published_after_march_2023.note: The paper is a preprint from July 2026.

summary: This paper introduces Humanity's Last Exam (HLE), a highly challenging multimodal benchmark consisting of 2,500 expert-written questions designed to test the absolute frontier of human knowledge across dozens of disciplines. By filtering out questions that current LLMs can easily answer, the benchmark provides a highly resistant test of expert academic capabilities, bridging mathematics, humanities, and sciences.
key_findings: Frontier models struggle significantly on HLE, with the highest-performing model (o3-mini) achieving only 13.4% accuracy. Furthermore, all evaluated models exhibit poor calibration, showing high calibration error (above 70% RMS calibration error) and frequently predicting incorrect answers with high confidence.
facets_explanation: The benchmark questions and reference answers were authored by over a thousand recruited domain experts (primarily professors, researchers, and graduate degree holders) who were subsequently offered co-authorship. Answering the questions requires highly specialized external graduate-level knowledge that is not contained in the stimulus. Divergence and expert disagreements were resolved through an iterative peer-review and rebuttal process until consensus was reached, treating divergence as noise to be minimized.
